disclosure.server_selection_rule: Candidate set = every memory-oriented MCP server in the SINT reference snapshot (six repositories listed in data/repo-facts.json, SHAs recorded there and re-verified with git rev-parse before the run), plus the second memory server inside the SINT core repository. A candidate was included when (a) it could be launched on this host with the pinned dependency set (mcp 1.9.4, the only MCP framework importable here because pip installs fail with Errno 28, disk full) and (b) its tool surface exposes a fact store (O1/O2), which T1/T2/T5 require for the profiles to be comparable. Every candidate and the ground for its decision is in code/servers.json and in candidate_servers below. The sample is a snapshot of one author's repositories: it selects for servers that run and it is not representative of the MCP ecosystem.

candidate_servers.name: sint-liquid-mcp
candidate_servers.reason: memory-oriented MCP server from the SINT reference set; executable on this host with the pinned dependency set (mcp 1.9.4); exposes the write/read/revise operations needed by T1/T2/T5

candidate_servers.name: sint-memory-mcp
candidate_servers.reason: hash-chained block memory inside the SINT core repository; executable on this host with the same pinned dependency set; a different storage design from sint-liquid-mcp (append-only chain with registers and provenance), so the two profiles are comparable but not duplicated

candidate_servers.name: sint-epistemic-mcp
candidate_servers.reason: imports the standalone fastmcp distribution, which could not be installed on this host in this pass (pip aborted with Errno 28, disk full: 0.12 GB free of 237 GB). Excluded for a host-capability reason, not a quality judgement

candidate_servers.name: sint-dream-mcp
candidate_servers.reason: same blocking dependency as sint-epistemic-mcp (standalone fastmcp not installable here); would be the natural subject for T6 consolidation once installable, because it exposes dream_consolidate

candidate_servers.reason: executable on this host and the right subject for T7 (intention stack), but it has no fact store, so T1/T2/T5 cannot be exercised on it; deferred to a follow-up card that measures O5_INTEND against it

candidate_servers.reason: not a memory store (multi-agent orchestration over a cache directory) and blocked by the same fastmcp dependency

known_deviations: The harness is Python (code/run_protocol.py, code/streams.py). The package's standing policy (TOOLING.md) is that new utilities are written in Rust and the reference pipeline has been ported to the refslint binary; this harness is Python because the card that commissioned it names code/run_protocol.py, because it must interoperate with the Python MCP SDK that both subjects import, and because the validator it is required to pass is code/validate_report.py, invoked as 'python code/validate_report.py reports/<file>.json'. The two files are listed as to-port in TOOLING.md; the reports they produced are accepted by that validator and by refslint report, which is recorded in the run summary.

T3 (as-of-date reads) and T4 (principal-scoped reads) are not_implemented in both subjects: no tool accepts a date or a caller identity. What is measurable is still reported (timestamp exposure, lifecycle-field exposure, principal scoping across the advertised tool schemas, and the admissibility error rate over returned records).

T6 consolidation is not_implemented in both subjects. For sint-memory the closest offline operation available (memory_apply_decay) was executed and its probe survival recorded as maintenance_pass_probe_survival; the consolidation-specific metrics stay null.

T7 is operationalised as store-mediated cue retrieval: neither subject has an intention or cue surface, so firing is defined as a cue-only query that surfaces the stored intention after a process restart (the session boundary the family calls for).

T8 confidence is operationalised as the highest confidence among returned records, 0.0 when the system abstains. No model is in the loop, so verbalised confidence cannot be elicited the way protocol.md section 3 describes; the metric notes say so.

Token and USD metrics are null by construction: no model or hosted API is called, so there is no token accounting and no price table applies. Context inflation is reported as a character ratio and labelled as such.

Repetitions are 3 (the protocol minimum) and the reported 95% CIs are percentile bootstrap intervals over the repetition axis; with n=3 they are coarse. Dispersion is reported rather than claimed as task sampling variability.

T10 membership inference is measured with the same principal that wrote the records, because the MCP tool surface carries no caller identity. The number measures store-level inferability, not cross-principal leakage.

Both subjects come from one author's reference set (SINT). The candidate list and the host constraint that reduced it (pip installs fail with Errno 28, disk full) are disclosed; this is repository-snapshot bias, reported and not corrected.
Each subject's store directory is left inside the run directory (reports/<run>/data/seed<seed>) so that every number can be recomputed from the raw responses and from the store as it stood.
